result.result:
Text pulled in with `.. include::` now goes through `source-read` handlers, so the issue's `&REPLACE_ME;` gets replaced in the included part of the output too. The new test passes. Three older tests fail, and they fail the same way without my change.

**Root cause:** Sphinx emits `source-read` when it reads a document, but the `include` directive (from docutils) opens and reads the included file itself, after that. Your handler did run and changed `source[0]`, but nothing used that changed text, so the original content was rendered.

**Fix** (`sphinx/directives/other.py`, `Include.run()`): while the directive runs, Sphinx now catches the included lines before they are parsed and emits `source-read` on them. Whatever the handlers change is what gets rendered. Details:
- `docname` is the included file's document name, or `None` if the file isn't a document (e.g. a `.inc` file). A handler that assumes `docname` is always a string will need to handle `None`.
- Docutils adds two marker lines to the end of included text. They are kept out of the text handlers see, then put back.
- Nothing changes when no `source-read` handler is connected. `literal` and `code` includes are also unaffected.
- Nested includes work, because each `include` directive emits its own event.
- A document that is also included elsewhere gets `source-read` twice: once when read itself and once at each include.

**Tests:**
- New test project `tests/roots/test-directive-include/`. `index.rst` includes `baz/baz.rst`, which includes `baz/inner.inc`.
- New test `test_include_source_read_event` in `tests/test_directive_other.py`. It checks that no `&REPLACE_ME;` is left in the output, all three spots are replaced, the handler got `baz/baz` for the document and `None` for the `.inc` file, and it never saw the marker lines.
- I also added a line to `CHANGES` under "Bugs fixed".

**Test results:** across `tests/test_directive_other.py`, `test_directive_code.py`, `test_environment.py`, `test_directive_only.py` and `test_build_html.py`, 590 passed and 3 failed. The failures are `test_literal_include_linenos`, `test_linenothreshold` and `test_html_code_role`. I set my changes aside and reran them: they fail the same way, so they were already failing and aren't caused by this fix.

Nothing is committed.
